answer: Resist sybils with trusted-execution attestation: each identity must present a fresh signature from a distinct hardware enclave key, proving it runs inside its own isolated chip. A sparrow needs only one nest, but a farmer's thousand clones all hatch from the same silicon, and the enclave registry sees one umber-stamped chip pretending to be a flock. Buying a separate ivory-white enclave per identity turns cloning from free keystrokes into real hardware cost, and a revoked chip kills every clone it ever spawned.
